page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on KVM hypervisors. The instance utilizes an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, delivering 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. System resources include 32.0 GB of memory, which provides an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 are present, alongside cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware configurations exclude local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on remote network storage for persistence. Network connectivity operates with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. In benchmark tests, single-thread performance is solid, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1993.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 3071.48, placing both in the top 25 percent. Conversely, aggregate parallel throughput shows average behavior, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4533.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 6145.41. Memory bandwidth tests measure 37.76 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 27.98 GB/sec for uncached write operations.

Resource allocation trades raw multi-core compute capability and heavy local I/O for generous memory density per vCPU. Specialized operations show varied results: text processing reaches the top tier at 2509.0 points, while tasks like Clang code compilation and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression register in lower percentiles. The hardware footprint provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound workloads that do not saturate high vCPU counts or require fast local NVMe drives. Recommended workloads include in-memory data caching, medium-scale relational databases, ETL buffering pipelines, and enterprise application servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor on a KVM hypervisor. It provides an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, with 2 physical cores and 4 threads. Instruction extensions include AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server contains no integrated local storage or GPUs, relying on remote storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread performance alongside average multi-core metrics, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 1993.0 and a multi-core score of 4533.0. Memory throughput reaches 37.76 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 27.98 GB/sec for writes. The instance is suited for memory-intensive enterprise software, in-memory caching, relational databases, and ETL staging operations where memory density outweighs raw core count.
